text: Autumn eighteen eighty-eight. Beneath the gaslights of Whitechapel, London held its breath.
Between August and November, five victims fell in the narrow alleys of the East End.
Scotland Yard flooded the streets, yet the killer left no face—only a name signed in blood.
From Hell. Then, as abruptly as the terror began, the footsteps vanished into the fog.
More than a century later, the block remains unfinished.
